To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) Orienters are not necessarily effective for learning prose, and (b) Orienters are most effective for learning prose when S’s task is to retain information, but least effective when S’s task involves recall of information.
Orienters are effective only when S is motivated and when the information is relevant to his needs.
Orienters may facilitate learning of prose material by (1) increasing the amount of information retained and (2) increasing the depth of processing of information.
